name: Header
statusNote: Header is an old, minimal component: three styled boxes with no responsive behaviour, menus or search. GitHub's production site header is built elsewhere; this one serves simple apps, and it has stayed alpha because little has been invested in it.
summary: GitHub's dark global bar: a horizontal row of items (logo link, navigation links, a full-width spacer item, avatar) on the header background. Choose it for an app-wide top bar; choose page-header for a page's own title block.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: Header.Item children, laid out left to right.

inputs.name: itemFull
inputs.description: Header.Item full: the item grows to take the free width, pushing later items to the end.

inputs.name: linkHref
inputs.description: Header.Link href (or a router location): a bold, unwrapped link in the logo colour, usually holding the mark and the product name.

anatomy.name: Bar
anatomy.description: A flex row on --header-bgColor in --header-fgColor-default, 16px padding on all sides, items centred vertically, no wrapping, horizontally scrollable when it overflows.

anatomy.name: Item
anatomy.description: A flex box stretched to the bar's content height, its content centred vertically, 16px after it.

anatomy.name: Link
anatomy.description: A flex link in --header-fgColor-logo at title weight, no underline, no wrapping, its icon and text centred.

layout.text: The bar is a non-wrapping flex row with 16px padding on all sides and items centred on the cross axis; its text is --text-body-size-medium at the --text-title-lineHeight-large line height. Its height is its tallest item plus 32px.
The bar overflows by scrolling horizontally rather than wrapping or collapsing items.
The bar stacks at z-index 32 so overlays and sticky content below it pass underneath.
Each item stretches to the bar's content height, centres its content vertically and keeps 16px after it (the last item too); a full item grows to fill the free width.
A link is a flex row of icon and text, centred, never wrapping, at --text-title-weight-large in --header-fgColor-logo.

states.text: A hovered link dims from --header-fgColor-logo to --header-fgColor-default.
A focused link (any focus, not only keyboard) dims the same way; the module draws no outline.

behaviour.text: A link navigates on activation; Header has no menus, collapse or responsive behaviour of its own.

accessibility.role: banner (a header element at page level)
keyboard: Tab moves through links and controls in the items in order.
semantics: The bar is a header element; at the top level of a page it is the banner landmark.
Links are named by their text, or by aria-label for an icon-only logo link.

notes.text: Hover and focus make the link dimmer, not brighter: --header-fgColor-default is white at 70% alpha, while --header-fgColor-logo is opaque.

The bar is dark in every theme (--header-bgColor is neutral 12 in light themes), so it pairs with the header foreground tokens, never the page's --fgColor-* tokens; controls placed in it need on-dark styling.
--header-borderColor-divider, --headerSearch-bgColor and --headerSearch-borderColor exist for GitHub's site header but nothing in this component reads them.
z-index 32 is a literal, not a --zIndex-* token.
No visible focus outline is drawn by the module (only the colour dims); a native build should add the standard --focus-outline-color ring on keyboard focus, as GitHub's global styles do.
Overflow is handled by overflow: auto, a horizontal scroll of the bar; a native build must clip the row and scroll it horizontally (or decide to collapse items, which Primer does not do).
Header.Link with a router location renders as the router's link; a native build navigates through the app's own router.
